why: Broadcom's own IR release confirms fiscal Q3 2026 results after the close on 2026-09-02 with a 14:00 PT call. Note the fiscal labelling: this is Q3 FY2026, not Q4.
session_evidence: amc: 'after the close of the market' 2026-09-02, call 14:00 PT - https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-inc-announce-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial
where_to_look: This is the most covered name of the day and the least room - do not spend the budget on the AI revenue guide, which forty analysts have modelled. The place where something unpriced can still live is the XPU customer roster: Broadcom discloses prospects and committed orders in aggregate, and the identities and order sizes are inferable from the hyperscalers' own capex disclosures and from supply-chain (CoWoS/HBM allocation) reporting

VMware: subscription conversion is now most of Infrastructure Software. The renewal cohort size and the churn from customers migrating off VMware are visible in competitor disclosures (Nutanix, Red Hat/IBM) and in enterprise licensing-dispute litigation dockets
Non-AI semiconductor recovery (broadband, wireless, industrial) is the segment consensus has largely written off; a turn there is the asymmetric line in the release
Gross-margin mix: XPUs carry lower margin than networking silicon, so a revenue beat with an adverse mix has twice produced a negative reaction (-12.6% in June 2026, -11.4% in December 2025)

The 7.9% event-implied move on a 2-day expiry with 193,971 contracts and a 3%-of-mid spread is the single most reliable priced-market statement in today's universe - use it as the benchmark, not as a finding
